newsitem.title: INDIA: One million Indian telecom workers begin strike.
newsitem.headline: One million Indian telecom workers begin strike.

text.p: About one million workers from India's state-owned telecommunications and postal departments began an indefinite nationwide strike over a wage dispute on Wednesday, a trade union leader said.

"A nationwide strike of over one million workers has begun and it is absolutely 100 percent," said Mallikarjun (one name), secretary-general of the Bharatiya (Indian) Telecom Employees' Federation, told Reuters.

Mallikarjun said the striking employees were demanding the abolition of a ceiling imposed by the government on annual bonus payments. New Delhi usually pays most junior employees an annual bonus during the Hindu festive season in October which is usually higher than the previous year.
However, the government had decided not to revise the payment upwards for its telecommunication and postal employees in 1996 as part of an austerity programme.
Mallikarjun said the employees were upset as the government had revised the bonus allowance for employees in the railways.

"When the government revised the scales for the railways they should not have left the telecom (employees) out ....," he said. "Now the ball is in their (the government's) court. Let the government decide and consider the demands of post and telegraph workers," he said.
